stemMarkdown: The price of an article is first increased by 11%, and then the new price is decreased by 38%. What is the net percentage change in price? (Enter a negative value if it is a net decrease.)
solutionMarkdown: Take the original price as 100. After a 11% increase: $100 \times (1 + 11/100) = 111.00$. After a 38% decrease on 111.00: $111.00 \times (1 - 38/100) = 68.82$. Net change $= 68.82 - 100 = -31.18\%$.
altSolutionMarkdown: Shortcut formula: net \% change $= p_1 - p_2 - \dfrac{p_1 p_2}{100} = 11 - 38 - \dfrac{418}{100} = -31.18\%$.
